overview: White develops the bishop to e3 instead of defending e4. After 3...dxe4 4.f3 (the Alapin-Diemer Gambit) White offers the e4 pawn for a lead in development and the open f-file, aiming for Nc3, Bd3, Qd2 and an attack. Black can keep the pawn with ...exf3 or ...Nf6 and usually gets an edge against accurate play, but White's play is easy to handle for club players.

white_ideas.idea: Recapture on f3 with Nxf3 and develop Nc3, Bd3 and Qd2
Use the f-file and the e5 push to attack the king
Castle long and push g4 and h4 against Black's kingside

black_ideas.idea: Take the pawn with ...exf3 and consolidate with ...Nf6 and ...c5
Trade queens or counterattack with ...c5 and ...Qb6
Develop quickly and meet f3 with ...Bd6

typical_structures.structure: Open centre with White pawns on d4 and f3 and an open e-file
Black extra pawn on d5 with a fragile White king-side

character.notes: White gambits a pawn for development and attack, and play is open and tactical.

gambit.notes: White gives up the e4 pawn on purpose and Black can keep it.

soundness.notes: Engines favour Black and the compensation is thought insufficient, though it scores through surprise.

structure.notes: Centre pawns come off and the pieces play on open files and diagonals.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom choose this gambit; it is picked for surprise.

level.notes: The attack is easy to play but Black must defend accurately; not a first repertoire line because it is dubious.

sublines_that_differ.name: Alapin-Diemer Gambit 4.f3
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e6 2. d4 d5 3. Be3 dxe4 4. f3
sublines_that_differ.how: The main gambit line; 3...Nf6 and 3...c5 avoid the gambit and are quieter.
